title: Tenali Rama and the cat who didn't want milk.
lines: This is a story from India, about clever Tenali Rama.
A king lived in the city of Vijayanagara.
His name was Krishnadevaraya.
He was a good king.
But there was a problem in his palace.
Mice!
Mice everywhere.
In the kitchen, in the cupboards, even in the king's bedroom.
They nibbled the bread.
They nibbled the rice.
They nibbled the queen's beautiful clothes.
This can't go on, said the king.
We need cats.
Lots of cats!
The king bought a thousand cats.
He gave one to every family in the city.
And with every cat the family also got a cow.
Because a cat needs milk, said the king.
Give your cat a bowl of milk every day.
Then she'll stay strong and catch lots of mice.
Tenali Rama got a cat too.
A grey one, with white paws.
And he got a lovely brown cow.
At home Tenali Rama looked at his cat.
She was sweet and she purred.
But Tenali Rama thought about it.
If I give my cat a big bowl of milk every day, he thought, she'll be full.
Then she won't be hungry anymore.
And then she won't catch a single mouse.
And the cow's milk?
I'd better give that to my children.
Or to the poor children from the street.
So Tenali Rama came up with a plan.
On the first day he put down a bowl of milk.
But it was a very hot bowl of milk.
Very hot, straight from the fire.
The cat was thirsty.
She put her tongue in the milk.
Ouch!
She burned her little tongue.
She jumped away.
Miaow!
From that day on the cat didn't like milk anymore.
When she saw a bowl of milk, she ran away.
She thought: Milk is hot.
Milk hurts.
And so she had to find her own food.
She caught mice.
Lots and lots of mice.
She became a very good hunter.
She was thin, but strong and fast.
And the cow's milk?
Tenali Rama gave it to his children and to the poor children from the street.
They drank milk every morning and grew big and strong.
A few months later the king wanted to know how the cats were doing.
Bring all the cats to the palace!
he said.
I want to see them.
All the families brought their cats to the palace.
The king looked at the cats.
They were fat.
Very fat.
They were so fat that they could hardly walk.
They lay lazily in the sun.
They yawned.
When a mouse ran past, they didn't even look up.
How lovely and fat they are!
said the king, pleased.
Well done, you gave them lots of milk.
Then Tenali Rama came with his cat.
His cat was thin.
She didn't have a fat tummy.
The king frowned.
Tenali Rama!
What have you done to your cat?
She's so thin!
Didn't you give her any milk?
Your Majesty, said Tenali Rama, my cat doesn't want to drink milk.
She doesn't like it.
The king laughed.
A cat that doesn't want milk?
There's no such thing!
Try it, Your Majesty, said Tenali Rama.
The king had a bowl of milk brought.
He put the bowl in front of Tenali Rama's cat.
But the cat looked at the milk and jumped away.
Miaow!
She ran right across the hall.
The king was amazed.
At that moment a mouse ran through the hall.
All the fat cats stayed lying down.
But Tenali Rama's cat jumped.
Hup!
She caught the mouse in one go.
All the courtiers clapped.
Tenali Rama told the king everything.
About the hot milk.
About the mice.
And about the milk he had given to the children.
Your Majesty, he said, a cat that gets too much becomes lazy.
But the children of our city really needed the milk.
The king thought about it.
Then he began to laugh.
Tenali Rama, you're clever!
You're right.
From now on we'll give the milk to the children.
And the cats can catch mice again.
And so the palace was soon free of mice.
And all the children of the city drank a cup of fresh milk every morning.
The end.
